title: Controlling the centre: count the attackers
outcomes: Counts the attackers of d4, e4, d5 and e5 for both sides
Picks the move that adds the most attackers to the central squares and names the pieces involved
Checks whether a central pawn can be held, and what is attacked, before playing for the centre

steps.text:
To **control** a square means your pawns and pieces attack it, and can win the fight there. A pawn standing on e4 or d4 *occupies* a central square; it controls only the squares it attacks.
Count attackers: for d4, e4, d5 and e5, how many pawns and pieces does each side have? More attackers is a first sign of control, not a verdict.

steps.caption: White to move. Watch the attackers on e5.

line.say: Nf3 attacks e5 (and d4). White has one attacker on e5.
Nc6 defends e5. Black has one defender of e5 and also attacks d4.
The d-pawn attacks e5 too. White now has two attackers on e5 against one defender.

claims.statement: After Nf3 White attacks e5 once.
After Nc6 Black defends e5 once.
After d4 White attacks e5 twice.

steps.text:
**Rule of thumb:** a central pawn controls squares only while it can be **held**. Count its attackers and defenders; if the count is against you, the pawn is a target, not control.
Capturing the enemy's central pawn is not automatic either: check what lines it opens. And what is attacked comes first: no plan beats losing a piece.

steps.title: Same pawns, one defender fewer
